content:
maya: Heads up — we started seeing a p99 latency spike in prod around 09:13 UTC right after the canary. p50 unaffected, but p99 jumped ~4x. Looks correlated with kernel-selector picking a fallback kernel under pressure.

leon: timeline? which routes/models? any metric diffs (batch size, kv hits)?

maya: model=redwood-13b-llama, route=/v1/generate, canary deploy at 09:10. Metric snapshots from 09:00->09:20: p99 480ms -> 2.1s, kv_cache_hit 82% -> 23%, avg_microbatch_size 3.1 -> 1.0, admission_rejection_rate up 7%.

ash: who rolled the kernel-selector change? we recently shipped a heuristic tweak to prefer "memory-friendly" kernels when free GPU memory < 4GB.

maya: that matches. logs show many decisions like: 
```
kernel_selector.choose(seq_len=1536, free_mem=3.2GB) -> fallback-matmul
kernel_selector.choose(seq_len=128, free_mem=3.2GB) -> fused-attn
```

leon: hm. fallback-matmul has higher per-token latency but lower memory. With smaller microbatches and low kv hits we're losing batching benefits -> increased latency. Can you grab a profiler? pprof or simple samples.

maya: attached a short pprof sample (saved to s3): s3://prod-profiles/1876543210/pprof.cpu.pb.gz. quick grep from sample: 
```
- fallback_matmul_kernel: 48% CPU samples
- batch_enqueue/serve_loop: 22%
- kv_cache_lookup: 8% (but hit path decreased)
```

kai: also check scheduler admission logic — looks like admission_control aggressively rejects queued microbatches when we hit memory pressure threshold. That collapses effective batch sizes to 1 which hurts fused kernels. Where did threshold move to?

anya: admission config in staging/prod: 
```
# previous: admission.memory_high_watermark = 0.85
# changed:  admission.memory_high_watermark = 0.70
```

ash: 0.70 is pretty aggressive. combined with kernel-selector preferring fallback when free_mem < 4GB, we end up serializing requests. two knobs collided.

leon: plan: rollback kernel-selector heuristic to previous commit and increase memory_high_watermark back to 0.85. also pin fused-attn preference for this model for 1 hour. who can roll?

anya: I can rollback the admission change and pin kernel selector flag. doing admission rollback now.

ops-bot: deploy rollback started by anya (deploy-id: d-8f3a). rolling back config: admission.memory_high_watermark -> 0.85.

anya: rolled back. pinned kernel-selector: `model.redwood-13b-llama.preferred_kernels = ["fused-attn"]` for canary cohort.

maya: after rollback (09:25) metrics show p99 -> 520ms, kv_cache_hit -> 79%, avg_microbatch_size -> 3.4. looks much better.

kai: good. next steps: add a safety check in kernel-selector that considers effective microbatch distribution and kv hit ratio before switching to high-latency fallback. heuristic sketch: 
```
if predicted_batch_size < 2 or kv_hit_rate < 0.5:
    prefer fused-attn even if memory tight (but keep OOM guard)
else:
    allow fallback-matmul
```

leon: also add an alert for rapid drop in kv_cache_hit concurrent with kernel change and admission change (so two-knob collisions show up).

ash: I'll open a short PR with tests that simulate low-memory + low-batch traffic and assert we don't flip to fallback when it causes tail blowups.

maya: thanks. putting a postmortem note into /incidents once PRs land. made a dashboard snapshot and pinned it to the thread: https://grafana.redwood/prod/d/latency/1876543210-kernel-mispick

anya: deploys completed. ops-bot shows config rollback success.

ops-bot: rollback finished (deploy-id: d-8f3a). health checks OK. :white_check_mark:

leon: great triage. capture timeline + config diff in the incident doc, include the pprof link and the microbatch distribution heatmap. small retrospective: two independent heuristics combined to cause the tail. we should treat kernel-selector + admission as a coupled surface.

maya: noted. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
